name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text: I’ll audit the memory graph for unembedded elements by running `grep -R --exclude-dir={.git,.vscode} -n "TODO\|FIXME\|@unembed" .` across the repo to surface raw notes and flags. I’ll then open the top 5 longest files in VS Code (`code $(ls -S | head -5)`) to manually inspect and embed the highest-value unreferenced chunks. If counts exceed 20, I’ll split the task into a separate branch labeled `memory/embed-<date>`.

name: Prune
text: Prune: "Graft’s audit risks conflating *temporary* flags (e.g., `@unembed` in WIP branches) with *structural* debt—how will you distinguish noise from signal? And if the top 5 longest files are monoliths, won’t manual embedding just surface more debt than it resolves? Where’s the triage criteria beyond file length?"
